summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn requests a successor experiment for the removed-leader finding under investigation d0b0ea6c28ce4d729188d4147e804657-question-0, using previous_id d0b0ea6c28ce4d729188d4147e804657-experiment with the revision reason that the basis changed: the harness now adds a post-window external-trigger phase and a third comparison, so the same two progress predicates are re-measured on the new basis together with the boundary of the stall. The retained comparison set is: with StepDownOnRemoval false the cluster must elect a new leader inside the fixed 80-round window without external help (expected violated), the StepDownOnRemoval true control must do so in the same window (expected holds), and the new boundary control requires that an eligible voter explicitly told to campaign takes leadership and a subsequent proposal commits (expected holds). Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, exactly that contrast plus the new control: the stalled cluster kept node 1 as StateLeader with no eligible leader and no index movement across the window, while after a single MsgHup on follower 2 an eligible node became leader and a proposal on it committed, and the step-down probe elected a leader inside the window on its own. The prefix, scope and assumptions state the tick schedule, the fault-free in-process delivery and the fact that the trigger is the same MsgHup path a forced election or operator action uses, so the executed record will show that the observed nonprogress is about the absence of an internal trigger rather than a permanently broken cluster. The formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
